title: Quantum Fisher Information Deficit as a Geometric Signature of Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking
abstract: Recently, strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB) has been established as a framework for describing quantum phases in open systems. However SW-SSB cannot be characterized by conventional charged two-point correlators. In this work, we show that, for strongly $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric states with local charged involutions, SW-SSB manifests as a persistent deficit from the maximal quantum Fisher information (QFI) under symmetry-neutral pair rotations. A model-independent inequality hierarchy establishes the equivalence of this deficit with fidelity and Rényi-1 correlators as asymptotic long-range-order diagnostics. It thereby connects finite-angle state overlaps to a constraint on the infinitesimal Bures geometry along the same pair-generated orbit. For symmetry-projected Gibbs states, we further derive a lower bound on the deficit governed by the mean energy injected by the pair operation. Crucially, locality keeps this energy cost uniformly bounded in system size and endpoint separation, maintaining a finite gap below the maximal QFI at any fixed finite temperature. When ordinary charged long range order is absent, this persistent geometric constraint provides a quantitative information-geometric characterization of thermal SW-SSB.
summary: This work introduces the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) deficit as a robust, geometric signature for detecting Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking in open quantum systems. By establishing an inequality hierarchy, the authors show this deficit is equivalent to the long-range order of other correlators. Crucially, they derive a thermal lower bound for this deficit, providing a quantitative measure of symmetry breaking even when conventional order parameters vanish.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of characterizing Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking (SW-SSB) in open quantum systems, where conventional two-point correlators fail.
main_result: It establishes that the QFI deficit provides a model-independent, quantitative information-geometric characterization of thermal SW-SSB, linking it to the long-range order of fidelity and Rényi-1 correlators.
method: The analysis employs the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) deficit, $D_s$, and derives an inequality hierarchy relating it to fidelity and Rényi-1 correlators, especially for symmetry-projected Gibbs states.
model_or_system: The study focuses on strongly $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric states with local charged involutions in open quantum systems, analyzing the system using pair-generated unitary orbits.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) deficit ($D_s$), root-fidelity correlator ($F_O$), and Rényi-1 correlator ($R_1$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($\beta$), system size, and the parameters governing the pair-generated unitary evolution.
main_assumptions: The results are derived for strongly $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric states with local charged involutions, and the thermal bound relies on specific inequalities.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry of neutral pair rotations and show the relationship between the QFI deficit and various correlators in different lattice geometries (e.g., ZXZ chain, 2D edge-dephasing).
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the QFI deficit as the diagnostic tool, establishes the inequality hierarchy relating $D_s$ to $F_O$ and $R_1$, then derives a lower bound for the deficit in thermal Gibbs states using injected energy, and finally applies this framework to specific lattice models.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, information-theoretic tool (QFI geometry) to detect subtle phases of matter (SW-SSB) in open systems where traditional order parameters break down, connecting quantum information measures to fundamental statistical physics concepts.
